paths.description: Homepage and primary news discovery surface; represents the main landing template.
Representative public news article; covers reading, metadata, article structure and newsletter UI.
Net Binnen listing; represents chronological section and listing templates.
Account sign-in journey reached from the primary header.
Deliberately invalid URL used to inspect HTTP failure and recovery presentation.

findings.summary: Non-JavaScript crawlers receive a privacy shell instead of news content
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched only 7,861 bytes, found 0% rendered-content coverage and identified a JS shell; the crawler screenshot contains no page content. Direct robots and sitemap requests were also blocked by the WAF from this audit origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve crawlable article and listing HTML without requiring the consent JavaScript round-trip, while keeping consent controls as enhancement.

findings.summary: The homepage has an extreme tracking and third-party footprint
findings.evidence: The tracker scan observed 45 third-party origins and 11 known tracker domains. The HAR attributed 108 of 117 requests and 11.41 MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors, gate non-essential analytics and advertising until valid consent, batch telemetry, and load media only on user intent.

findings.summary: Core news content is unavailable without JavaScript
findings.evidence: The raw-HTML discoverability comparison found 0% content overlap, no raw title, h1 or description, and classified the response as a JavaScript shell/privacy gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Render core headlines and article content in the initial HTML, then enhance consent, ads and account features with JavaScript.

findings.summary: Media and third parties dominate the page budget
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 11.41 MB across 108 requests, including 8.44 MB of live video, which is disproportionate for a news landing page before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit third-party and media budgets, lazy-load video, and remove vendors that do not provide commensurate user value.

findings.summary: Long-running motion continues under reduced-motion
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched, the probe still found seven 1.5s livefeed-pulse animations and two 121.34s ticker/swap animations running.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential pulse, ticker and swap animations in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query and replace auto-motion with a static state.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly exposed on primary navigation
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline:none and no box shadow on the main navigation links; it also found 29 of 80 sampled targets below 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible with a high-contrast outline and enlarge compact controls to meet practical touch target guidance.

findings.summary: The sign-in journey ends at a blocked state
findings.evidence: Following the header sign-in action redirects to login2.ad.nl and produces “Inlogpoging geblokkeerd” with HTTP-like status 406, so the primary account journey cannot complete in this session.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep a working code-based sign-in path available from the blocked state and provide a direct retry/back action rather than instructions alone.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers an excessive 11.67 MB on load
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 117 requests and 11,668,883 transferred bytes; 8.44 MB came from live-streaming video segments, while Lighthouse flagged redirects, cache lifetime, document latency and render blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not fetch the live stream until the player is visible or explicitly started; improve cache lifetimes and first-document delivery.

findings.summary: News images and a newsletter field lack accessible alternatives
findings.evidence: The images primitive reported missing alt on all 100 sampled images. The form probe found the first email input had no associated label or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide meaningful alt text or empty alt for decorative images and programmatically label every input.

findings.summary: Focus treatment and heading semantics are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order and accessible-name/visible-label matching; the focus probe found no visible outline on sampled primary links.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore sequential heading structure, align accessible names with visible labels, and add consistent :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP defaults weaken otherwise strong transport security
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; 25 of 27 cookies were reported without Secure, including long-lived analytics identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based CSP, remove unsafe-eval, and set Secure plus the narrowest viable SameSite policy on every HTTPS cookie.

findings.summary: Account access is not recoverable from the blocked screen
findings.evidence: The sign-in endpoint shows a status 406 block and textual instructions but no visible control to return, switch to email-code sign-in, or retry.
findings.suggestedFix: Place direct recovery actions on the blocked page and verify the complete email-code and account-management journey.

findings.summary: An offscreen live stream downloads megabytes without user intent
findings.evidence: The HAR shows ten live-streaming requests transferring 8.44 MB during a six-second homepage capture, despite no player being visible in the first desktop or mobile viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer stream manifests and segments until the player intersects the viewport or the user presses play.

findings.summary: The initial page has a very large DOM and heap footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 872,921 nodes, 3,637,944 edges and 53,675,080 self-size bytes, high for a news landing page before extended interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise or defer below-fold modules, release advertising/video state, and avoid constructing the full 18,000px page at startup.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-equivalent to the light capture, and computed html color-scheme remains normal with a light #f6f6f6 surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide dark surface, text and media treatments with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reserved advertising space delays visible content
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots devote roughly the first 390px below navigation to blank advertising space before the leading story, reducing content density.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse empty advertising containers promptly and reserve only the space required for ads that will render.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP misses the good threshold in the redirected first-visit path
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.6s LCP and 2.6s FCP on the consent redirect path. A direct trace was better at 2.19s LCP, showing the redirect/first-visit path is the risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove avoidable redirect latency and prioritise the actual LCP resource on first visit.

findings.summary: Third-party and unused JavaScript add avoidable cost
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 38 scripts and Lighthouse estimated 58 KiB unused JavaScript; video player, tag manager, experimentation and advertising libraries all load on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load advertising, experimentation and video code only when the corresponding feature becomes relevant.

findings.summary: Many controls are too compact for reliable touch use
findings.evidence: At 360px the page reflows without overflow, but the target probe found 29 of 80 sampled interactive elements under 24px in width or height.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas around compact header, utility and live-feed controls without changing visual density.

findings.summary: Some images do not reserve intrinsic space
findings.evidence: The images primitive found five images without explicit dimensions and five without srcset; Lighthouse also failed the unsized-images audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height or aspect-ratio to every content image and provide responsive sources.

findings.summary: Browser diagnostics report lifecycle and inspector problems
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported DevTools Inspector issues and three BFCache failure reasons on the first-visit route.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the recorded Inspector issues and remove unload/lifecycle blockers that prevent BFCache restoration.

findings.summary: The authentication surface offers no observable phishing-resistant sign-in
findings.evidence: The sign-in route is blocked and only describes email-code authentication; no passkey or WebAuthn UI could be reached or observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys as a primary or upgrade authentication option while retaining email-code recovery.

findings.summary: Defensive policies remain overly permissive
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, DENY framing and strict-origin referrer policy, but CSP allows unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval and Permissions-Policy only declares two client-hint features.
findings.suggestedFix: Tighten CSP and explicitly disable unneeded powerful features in Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Published times are not machine-readable or locale-robust
findings.evidence: Article time elements use human text such as “18 juli 2026, 14:52” and “Laatste update: 16:08” directly in datetime rather than valid ISO date/time values; no Intl usage was observed in the rendered article.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit valid ISO datetime attributes and format visible dates through Intl.DateTimeFormat for the active locale.

findings.summary: Email fields omit autocomplete assistance
findings.evidence: Both sampled newsletter email inputs reported an empty autocomplete value; the first also lacked a programmatic label.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete="email", stable names, inputmode where useful, and preserve browser autofill.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The modern CSS probe found no view-transition CSS or authored startViewTransition integration even though the homepage exposes many document navigations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document or same-document View Transitions for meaningful route changes, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages lack scroll-state-aware navigation cues
findings.evidence: The homepage is 18,403px tall, while the CSS signal probe found no scroll-state queries, progress indicator, or authored scroll-timeline cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/scroll progress cue or scroll-state-aware header treatment, respecting reduced motion.
